newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-NHLERS ADDED TO WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP ROSTERS.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-NHLERS ADDED TO WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP ROSTERS.

text.p: The United States finalized their ice hockey world championship roster on Thursday with the addition of St. Louis Blues winger Jim Campbell.

A candidate for NHL rookie of the year honours, Campbell collected 23 goals and 43 points for the Blues, who were knocked out of the first round of the NHL playoffs on Sunday by the Detroit Red Wings.
Finland also completed their lineup by adding three players - but not the three coach Curt Lindstrom had wanted.
It was confirmed Thursday that Phoenix Coyotes Teppo Numminen, described by Lindstrom as one of the top 10 defencemen in the NHL, will join the team Friday in time for their game against Slovakia.
Lindstrom however, did not get the help up front he was seeking when NHL forwards Sami Kapanen of the Hartford Whalers and Dallas Stars Jere Lehtinen were ruled out because of injuries.

The Finns will also have to do without Anaheim sniper Teemu Selanne, who had 51 goals this season, and veteran Jari Kurri after the Mighty Ducks won their opening series and advanced to the second round.
Instead Lindstrom has added Finnish league all-stars Antti Tormanen and Antti Aalto to the squad.
Russia's hopes of winning their first world championship medal in four years received a major boost with Ottawa Senators' Alexei Yashin agreeing to join the team.

Yashin, one of the NHL's top power forwards, led the Senators in scoring this season with 35 goals and 75 points, and is expected to be in uniform Saturday for Russia's final round-robin match against Finland.
The Senators lost their opening playoff series 4-3 to the Buffalo Sabres.
